events.title: Labour Unrest Spreads
events.description: Strikes and demonstrations are building around a grievance that's gone unaddressed too long. The Interior Ministry wants a decision.

options.label: Crack down on the unrest
options.description: Riot police clear the demonstrations. Order returns fast, at a cost to your standing with the streets and the wider public.

options.label: Negotiate with organizers
options.description: Open a direct channel with strike leaders and offer concessions. Costs the treasury, buys goodwill.

options.label: Let it run its course
options.description: You take no action. The unrest simmers a while longer and public patience wears thin.

events.title: Shots on the Ceasefire Line
events.description: A patrol traded fire across the line last night. Nobody died, both sides say the other started it, and the ceasefire nobody signed in good faith held by about forty minutes. Foreign Affairs is waiting on your response.

options.label: Lodge a formal protest
options.description: A stern note through the usual channels. Firm, restrained, and unlikely to satisfy anyone who lost a cousin in 1992.

options.label: Name them from the podium
options.description: Say out loud what everyone believes about who armed the separatists. The chamber will love it. The embassy will not.

options.label: Seek quiet de-escalation
options.description: Back-channel talks, no cameras, no communiqué. Cheaper than the alternative and impossible to claim credit for.

events.title: Cabinet Corruption Exposé
events.description: An investigative report alleges a minister used their office for personal gain. The story is spreading fast.

options.label: Publicly defend the minister
options.description: You back your minister publicly. If the story holds up, this could look very bad later.

options.label: Ask for a quiet resignation
options.description: A minister steps down before the story can grow. A brief embarrassment, then it passes.

options.label: Launch an independent inquiry
options.description: Slower, more credible, and out of your hands once it starts.

events.title: Bumper Harvest
events.description: An unusually strong harvest has left the country with a real, if modest, surplus. A rare piece of good news for the Economy Ministry to manage.

options.label: Stockpile the surplus
options.description: Bank the gains against leaner years ahead.

options.label: Export the surplus
options.description: Sell abroad for quick revenue.

options.label: Subsidize consumer prices
options.description: Pass the windfall straight to households.

events.title: Currency Speculators Circle
events.description: Investors are testing the currency's resolve, betting on either inflation or debt forcing your hand. Finance wants direction.

options.label: Raise interest rates sharply
options.description: Defends the currency, chokes growth.

options.label: Impose capital controls
options.description: Blunt and unpopular with investors, but it buys room to breathe.

options.label: Ride it out
options.description: Let the market find its own level. Risky if it doesn't stop on its own.

events.title: A Rival's Scandal
events.description: An opposition figure has been caught in an embarrassing scandal of their own. How you handle it is entirely your call.

options.label: Press the political advantage
options.description: Hammer the story in the press. Good for you, ugly politics.

options.label: Stay above the fray
options.description: Say nothing. Voters may reward the restraint — or may not notice at all.

events.title: Trade Route Disruption
events.description: The corridors the Union built all run the wrong way for an independent country, and one of them has just closed. Your busiest trade relationship is rippling. Someone will feel the pinch.

options.label: Absorb the cost domestically
options.description: Subsidize affected industries directly rather than let supply chains break.

options.label: Let prices adjust
options.description: Let the market absorb the shock. Cheaper for the state, harder on households.

events.title: Run on the Provincial Bank
events.description: Depositors are queueing around the block at one of the country's larger banks. If the panic spreads to the rest of the system, this stops being one bank's problem.

options.label: Guarantee all deposits
options.description: The treasury stands behind every account. Expensive, but the queues disperse by evening.

options.label: Arrange a private rescue
options.description: Twist the arms of the big banking houses to absorb their failing rival. Cheaper for the state; the bankers will remember the favour they did you.

options.label: Let it fail
options.description: Depositors take the loss and the panic burns through the economy.

options.label: Stake your reputation on the numbers
options.description: You ran monetary policy for a decade. Go on television with the balance sheet and dare the panic to argue with you.

events.title: Strike Wave
events.description: Walkouts are spreading plant to plant — pay packets can't keep up, and the unions smell weakness. The next few days decide whether this stays economic or becomes political.

options.label: Negotiate a wage deal
options.description: Buy industrial peace with a settlement. Costs the budget, calms the shop floor.

options.label: Hold firm
options.description: No concessions under pressure. The unions may fold — or escalate.

options.label: Clear the picket lines
options.description: Order and open gates by the weekend — and a wound that will fester.

options.label: Speak to them as one of their own
options.description: You carried a union card before you carried a red box. Walk in without minders and settle it the old way.

events.title: General Strike
events.description: It happened: the unions have called everyone out. Ports, rails, mills — the country is standing still, and everyone remembers how you handled the first wave.

options.label: Concede the unions' demands
options.description: End it today at the treasury's expense.

options.label: Wait them out
options.description: Strikers don't get paid either. A grinding month for everyone.

options.label: Declare essential-services orders
options.description: Force the ports and power stations open by decree. Effective, authoritarian, unforgotten.

options.label: Put the ports under military control
options.description: Not a review, not an order — soldiers on the docks by morning. Only a leader of your temperament would dare.

events.title: Revenue Windfall
events.description: The mid-year figures are in and the treasury has collected meaningfully more than forecast. Everyone in cabinet has a plan for it by lunchtime.

options.label: Pay down debt
options.description: Quietly responsible.

options.label: Announce public works
options.description: Visible cranes in every district by spring.

options.label: A one-off tax rebate
options.description: Cheques in the post with the government's compliments.

events.title: A Deputy Crosses the Floor
events.description: A sitting deputy has renounced their party whip live on the evening news, citing 'a crisis of conscience'. Their old party wants blood; every other party wants the seat.

options.label: Court the defector
options.description: A warm handshake for the cameras — and their vote, most days.

options.label: Stay out of it
options.description: Party quarrels are best watched from a safe distance.

events.title: The Government Retreats
events.description: After weeks of pressure, the government has abandoned one of its headline proposals. You cannot issue orders from opposition — but you can decide what political meaning the retreat will carry.

options.label: Claim the retreat as your victory
options.description: Put your front bench on every broadcast and argue that sustained opposition forced the reversal.

options.label: Publish the alternative
options.description: Use the opening to explain what your party would do instead. A slower gain, but a stronger claim to be ready for office.

options.label: Let the government own its confusion
options.description: Say little and trust voters to notice. Most will not.

events.title: A By-Election Opening
events.description: A vacant constituency has produced an unexpected contest. This is not a decision about the country; it is a test of how your opposition party spends its limited people, money, and attention.

options.label: Turn it into a national referendum
options.description: Flood the district with organisers and make the government defend its national record.

options.label: Run a disciplined local campaign
options.description: Keep the leader away, select a credible local voice, and build the organisation for the general election.

options.label: Conserve resources
options.description: Save the war chest for the national contest and surrender the initiative today.

events.title: The Procurement Files
events.description: A newspaper has published a cache of documents suggesting ministry contracts have been steered to friends of officials for years. The story has a name, a logo, and no intention of going away.

options.label: Order a full public inquiry
options.description: Let the chips fall. Credible — and once it starts, it doesn't answer to you.

options.label: Sack the named officials
options.description: Swift, visible, and conveniently shallow.

options.label: Ride it out
options.description: Newspapers need a new front page every day. Eventually.

options.label: Take the brief yourself
options.description: You argued before the high court for twenty years. Stand at the podium, walk the country through the evidence, and make the case no hired counsel could.

events.title: The Procurement Trial Verdict
events.description: The inquiry you ordered has ended in court, and the verdict lands today. Senior officials are going to prison — including two appointed under your government's watch.

options.label: Welcome the verdict
options.description: Justice done, whatever it costs the government's friends.

options.label: Arrange quiet pardons
options.description: Loyalty repaid — if it stays quiet, which these things never do.

events.title: The Court Strikes Back
events.description: The high court has ruled a pillar of the government's legislative programme unconstitutional in part. The justices are daring you to make it a fight.

options.label: Comply with the ruling
options.description: Rule of law means losing gracefully sometimes.

options.label: Denounce the court
options.description: 'Unelected judges against the people's government.' The base loves it; the institutions do not.

events.title: The Chairman's Offer
events.description: The owner of the country's largest media group requests a private dinner. Over dessert he offers 'a fairer hearing' for the government — and mentions, in passing, a broadcasting regulation he'd like relaxed.

options.label: Reach an understanding
options.description: Warmer coverage within the week. He will collect eventually.

options.label: Decline politely
options.description: Dinner was excellent; the answer is no.

events.title: A Spy in the Ministry
events.description: Counter-intelligence has caught an agent inside the defence ministry. The handler is known to them — the networks the old Union left behind were never rolled up, only reassigned. How loudly do you want this to get?

options.label: Expel their diplomats
options.description: A public row, embassy staff on the next flight home.

options.label: Handle it quietly
options.description: A discreet démarche and a traded prisoner. The public never knows.

options.label: Turn the agent
options.description: Feed them what you want believed. Risky, invisible, delicious.

events.title: Refugees at the Border
events.description: A neighbour's civil war has arrived at your frontier: thousands of families with everything they own on their backs. The border guards are asking for orders.

options.label: Open the border
options.description: Do the decent thing and absorb the cost — economic and political.

options.label: Build border camps
options.description: Shelter without settlement — the compromise that satisfies no one.

options.label: Seal the border
options.description: Turn them back. The pictures will be terrible.

events.title: The Integration Question
events.description: Months on, the families you admitted are settling in — and the question of work permits, schools, and citizenship has reached the floor of the assembly, trailed by every prejudice in the country.

options.label: Fast-track work permits
options.description: New taxpayers by year's end; new voters someday.

options.label: A cautious, staged path
options.description: Reviews, quotas, and committees. Slow satisfies the middle.

events.title: The Students Are Marching
events.description: A student movement has grown out of the universities — idealistic, loud, and photogenic. Their demands are a mix of the impossible and the overdue.

options.label: Meet their leaders
options.description: Tea, cameras, and one achievable concession.

options.label: Dismiss them as naive
options.description: 'They'll grow up.' Their parents vote, though.

events.title: Faith and State
events.description: A dispute over religious symbols in public schools has escalated from a local quarrel into a national argument about what kind of country this is.

options.label: Hold a firm secular line
options.description: The state has no favourite gods.

options.label: Defend tradition
options.description: Some things predate the republic and will outlast it.

options.label: Leave it to local councils
options.description: Federalism: the art of making problems someone else's.

events.title: The River Breaks Its Banks
events.description: A week of rain has put three districts underwater. Farms, mills, and homes are gone; the cameras are already there, and so must you be.

options.label: Full national mobilisation
options.description: Army engineers, emergency housing, a visibly present government.

options.label: Standard relief effort
options.description: Competent, procedural, forgettable.

events.title: A Shot Outside the Assembly
events.description: A gunman was wrestled down metres from a cabinet minister this morning. Nobody was hurt — this time. The security services want sweeping new powers by tonight.

options.label: Grant the sweeping powers
options.description: Safer streets, colder civil liberties.

options.label: A measured security review
options.description: Fix the failures without rewriting the constitution overnight.

options.label: A soldier's composure
options.description: You've been shot at by professionals. Walk the same route tomorrow, unhurried, and let the country draw its own conclusion.

events.title: A Challenge From Within
events.description: Your own party's leading wing has run out of patience with you. A letter with too many signatures is circulating, and tonight's party meeting has one unwritten agenda item: whether you still speak for them.

options.label: Face them down
options.description: Walk into the meeting alone and remind them who wins them elections. It works — this time — and it costs them nothing to hate you quietly.

options.label: Bend toward the wing
options.description: Adopt half their platform as your own. Cheaper than a war — but you become a little more like them.

options.label: Purge the ringleaders
options.description: Deselect them, demote them, brief against them. The wing shrinks; the whole party remembers how.

events.title: Another Week on the Line
events.description: The ceasefire holds the way it always holds. This week it was the usual: shooting across the contact line that both sides insist began with the other, a dispute over men held since 1992, and a Krasovan 'peacekeeping' convoy on a road it has no business using. The Foreign Ministry wants to know how loudly to object.

options.label: Absorb it and say nothing
options.description: Log the violation, brief nobody, move on. It costs nothing this week and a little of something harder to name.

options.label: Protest through the mediators
options.description: Put it on the record with the monitors and the embassies. Nothing changes on the ground, but the file grows, and one day the file may matter.

options.label: Respond in kind
options.description: Return fire, close the road, hold their convoy at the checkpoint for a day. The line quietens for a fortnight afterwards. It always does. It never lasts.

events.title: Someone Offers to Mediate
events.description: A delegation from the international monitors has asked for a meeting, and everyone knows what about. After a year of incidents on the line, there is an appetite abroad for a framework — and the quiet suggestion that if Ardenia will not discuss one, others will discuss it without her. The chamber has been arguing about Vetrenka since before this government existed. Now it has to decide.

options.label: Enter the peace process
options.description: Negotiate in good faith, with mediators in the room and the possibility of an outcome nobody in the chamber has publicly accepted. Slow, expensive, and the only path that closes this.

options.label: Prepare to retake the region
options.description: Reject the framework, mobilise, and finish the war the State Council lost. The army is not what it was in 1992 — and neither, everyone assumes, is the force waiting on the other side.

options.label: Freeze it properly
options.description: Accept the line as an administrative fact without ever saying the word recognition. Trade resumes, the shooting mostly stops, and a fifth of the country stays gone for as long as anyone can see.

events.title: The Framework Is Initialled
events.description: It took eleven months, four venues and a formula on the status question so carefully worded that both delegations were able to tell their capitals they had won. The shooting stops. The displaced get a mechanism. Nobody gets to say the word they wanted to say.

options.label: Sign it
options.description: Put your name on the thing that ends it, and accept that the name on it will be the one history argues about.

events.title: The Talks Collapse
events.description: They collapsed over the sequencing of a paragraph nobody outside the room could explain. What everyone understood was the photograph of the empty table, and the fact that the government spent a year of its authority on it and came home with the paragraph unresolved.

options.label: Blame them and walk away
options.description: Publish your version first. The line goes back to what it was, only colder, and next time the mediators call somebody else will take the meeting.

events.title: The Flag Over Vetrenka
events.description: Nine days, further than anyone in the ministry privately expected, and the separatist command has withdrawn across the water rather than be encircled. Ardenian troops are in the regional capital. What the pictures do not show is the third of the population that left with them, and the fact that the region is now a place your army has to hold.

options.label: Hold it and govern it
options.description: Occupation, administration, reconstruction, and an insurgency that has simply changed address.

events.title: The Offensive Breaks
events.description: It went wrong on the second day and comprehensively by the fourth. Krasovan aircraft were over the corridor within a week — 'protecting peacekeepers', a phrase their foreign ministry had clearly prepared some time ago. The line is now further inland than it was, and the government is explaining why.

options.label: Take the ceasefire offered
options.description: Sign what is put in front of you, on worse terms than the one you rejected, and survive the week.

events.title: A Line on the Map, Quietly
events.description: No treaty, no ceremony, no word said aloud. Customs posts become permanent, the crossing reopens on published hours, and the official maps go to the printers with a dotted line where a border is not. The National Conservatives have called it the second February Intervention, which is unfair, and effective.

options.label: Let it stand
options.description: Say nothing, sign nothing, change nothing. The cheapest thing this government will ever do, and the one it will be remembered for.

modifiers.source: A Line on the Map, Quietly

events.title: The Crossing Opens on Schedule
events.description: Five months on, the extraordinary has become the timetable. Lorries queue at the crossing on published hours, families visit on day permits, and the argument about what to call the line has moved from the chamber to the letters page. Nobody has forgiven it. Everybody has stopped organising against it.

options.label: Say nothing and let it settle
options.description: Do not defend it, do not repeat it, do not give it a name. It survives on being boring.

events.title: "Who Gave It Away?"
events.description: The National Conservatives have found their campaign and it is a single question, asked at every rally, printed on every leaflet, put to every minister who steps outside. Veterans' associations have joined it. So, quietly, have people who voted for this government. There is no rebutting the question, because the answer is you.

options.label: Ride it out
options.description: Take the losses, refuse the fight you cannot win, and hope the question gets old before the government does.

events.title: The West Is Talking Again
events.description: A customs post in the western districts was raided in the night — weapons taken, nobody hurt, nobody caught. Two days later a recording surfaced in the markets: an older man's voice, unhurried, talking about a republic that was stolen twice. The Interior Ministry will not say on the record that it is Dorin Vasca. They will not say it isn't.

options.label: Send the security services west
options.description: Sweep the districts, arrest the network, finish what the Turn of the Year left undone. If the ministries are up to it. They may not be.

options.label: Offer terms to the rank and file
options.description: Amnesty for anyone who walks out of the hills by spring; nothing at all for Vasca himself. Isolate the man from the grievance. The National Conservatives will call it surrender before you finish announcing it.

options.label: Call it banditry and move on
options.description: A criminal matter for the district police. Say the name as little as possible; a ghost you refuse to discuss is still a ghost, and cheaper this month.

options.label: Go west and run it yourself
options.description: You commanded men in that country once. Take the operation personally, and take the consequences personally with it.

events.title: They Took Him Near the Border
events.description: It was ordinary in the end. A roadblock, a car that turned around too slowly, and an old man in the back seat who gave a false name to soldiers young enough to be his grandchildren. He asked to be allowed to walk to the vehicle himself. They let him.

options.label: Try him in open court
options.description: Everything on the record, in front of the cameras, for as long as it takes. It will be ugly, and it will be the most convincing thing this republic has done.

modifiers.source: They Took Him Near the Border

options.label: Hold him quietly
options.description: No trial, no platform, no martyr. Also no answer to the question of what kind of state does that.

events.title: The Sweep Comes Back Empty
events.description: Three weeks, four districts, two hundred arrests and not one of them him. What the operation did find was every family in the west with a story about soldiers in their kitchen at four in the morning. Recruitment in the hills has never been easier.

options.label: Go back in harder
options.description: Double the deployment and accept what that means. The alternative is admitting the first attempt was a mistake, which is politically worse and factually true.

options.label: Withdraw and say little
options.description: Pull the units back to barracks and let the story die of boredom. The west remains the west.

events.title: They Come Down From the Hills
events.description: Not all of them, and not at once. But through the spring they came down in ones and twos — men who had been fighting for a president nobody had seen in a year, and who wanted, mostly, to go home. What is left up there is smaller than it was, older, and no longer an army.

options.label: Write the amnesty into law
options.description: Make it permanent and make it public, so the next man who considers the hills knows exactly what the door back looks like.

modifiers.source: They Come Down From the Hills

options.label: Take the win quietly
options.description: No ceremony, no legislation, no chance for anyone to make a speech about it. Some victories keep better in the dark.

events.title: He Used the Winter
events.description: The amnesty emptied the fringes of his movement and left the core of it — and the core, it turns out, was what mattered. They spent the quiet months organising. The customs posts are being hit again, competently this time, by men who know which nights the patrols change.

options.label: Reinforce and contain
options.description: Hold the district boundaries, protect the posts, and accept that this is now a standing commitment rather than a problem you are solving.

options.label: Offer him terms directly
options.description: Stop pretending he is a criminal matter and treat him as what he is: a man with a following, who might yet be bought with something other than money.

events.title: A Government That Does Not Look
events.description: Calling it banditry worked for about a season. It is harder now: the western districts have stopped forwarding tax receipts, two district administrators have resigned citing their families, and the recording in the markets has been followed by three more. He is no longer denying it is him.

options.label: Act now, late
options.description: Everything the security option would have cost in the autumn, plus a year of him recruiting on your indifference.

options.label: Still not a national question
options.description: Say nothing again. The west is a long way from Vashtera and the budget is due.

modifiers.source: A Government That Does Not Look

events.title: The Compound at Drevna
events.description: They have him located — a farm compound above the Drevna valley, thirty or forty men, and a road in that can be watched but not easily driven. For the first time since the Turn of the Year, the government knows where Dorin Vasca is sleeping. What happens next is a decision, not an intelligence problem.

options.label: Take the compound
options.description: Go in before dawn and end it. Whatever is written about how it ended will be written afterwards, by people who weren't there.

options.label: Offer him a plane
options.description: Safe passage, a third country, and a public statement that costs him more than prison would. He is old and he is tired and he has read the same histories you have.

options.label: Watch the road and wait
options.description: Do nothing, keep the compound under observation, and let the question stay open for whoever governs next.

events.title: A Minister Is Counting Votes
events.description: Your whips report a pattern: one of your ministers has been holding meetings that appear on no diary, with people who have no business in their department. Nothing provable. Everything obvious.

options.label: Confront them privately
options.description: Summon them, alone, and let them know you know. It forces their hand — one way or the other.

options.label: Let it play out
options.description: Say nothing. Watch who visits them. A plot you can see is worth more than one you've driven underground — until it isn't.

events.title: The Minister Denies Everything
events.description: They sat across from you and denied all of it, pleasantly, for forty minutes. Then, at the door, they mentioned how many colleagues share their concerns about the government's direction. It was not a threat. It was an invoice.

options.label: Pay the invoice
options.description: Give them the brief they want and the standing that comes with it. They will be loyal, and they will never forget that you blinked.

options.label: Demand their resignation
options.description: End it now, publicly, while you still hold the initiative. Their allies will not forgive it.

events.title: The Numbers Are Real
events.description: You let it run, and now you can see the shape of it: a bloc of names, a date, and a candidate. Your minister has stopped pretending to count and started pretending to be reluctant.

options.label: Break them now, whatever it costs
options.description: Sack them and everyone who signed. It works. The party will be smaller and angrier, and so will you.

options.label: Put the whole thing in the papers
options.description: Brief the lobby correspondents yourself. Plots die in daylight — and so does the fiction that your house is in order.

options.label: There is nothing left to do
options.description: You have no votes to spare and no time to find them. It happens now, and it happens to you.

events.title: Your Minister Has the Numbers
events.description: It is done in a committee room with the lights on. Your minister has the signatures, the press has the story, and the party has a question to answer about who leads it.

options.label: Give ground and survive
options.description: Concede the policy, keep the office, and let them believe they won. Most of politics is deciding what losing looks like.

options.label: Make them do it in the open
options.description: No deal. Let them table the motion and count the votes in front of the cameras. You may lose. They will bleed either way.

events.title: The Valve, With a Date
events.description: The supplier's gas company has put it in writing: unless the arrears come down, deliveries through the Zovar line fall next month. The Finance Ministry can find some hard currency. Not much, and not twice.

options.label: Pay enough to take the date off the table
options.description: Hard currency the treasury does not have, paid in tranches until the arrears are below the line their lawyers named.

options.label: Buy a spot cargo and let them cut
options.description: A tanker at a premium, so the cut lands on an empty pipe instead of cold flats.

options.label: Take the letter to the Western embassies
options.description: Make the threat a story about them, not us. The supplier will not enjoy reading it.

options.label: Call the bluff
options.description: They have mentioned the valve before. Say nothing, and see whether they mean it this time.

events.title: Whose Pipe Is It?
events.description: The supplier says the Zovar transit fees were set for a friendlier decade and wants them gone. Its gas company has started paying late, and the Foreign Ministry hears the word 'review' a great deal.

options.label: Concede the fees for a better price
options.description: Give up the transit revenue for good, and take a cheaper contract until the next renewal.

options.label: Ask the Western institutions to arbitrate
options.description: A neutral panel in a Western capital. The supplier will call it a provocation and attend anyway.

options.label: Hold the fees where they are
options.description: The treaty says what it says. Read it to them slowly.

events.title: A Cold Winter in Someone Else's Country
events.description: Gas through the Zovar line is running above contract on its way west, and the transit fees with it. The Finance Ministry has a sum it did not budget for and three ministers who know what to do with it.

options.label: Pay down the debt
options.description: Nobody thanks a government for a debt figure, but the next ISF review will.

options.label: A heating rebate for the coldest regions
options.description: Money back on the winter bill, delivered before anyone has to ask.

options.label: Put it toward gas storage
options.description: Start the storage programme with someone else's money. The next valve threat will be quieter.

events.title: The Fund Says No
events.description: The ISF mission has failed the quarterly review. The disbursement is suspended, the Bank's governor is not taking calls, and the markets have done the arithmetic. The mission chief is still in the capital.

options.label: Renegotiate the programme
options.description: The tranche comes back, the targets tighten, and the bank condition moves later. Everyone will know who asked.

options.label: Announce a spending freeze
options.description: A year of frozen budgets, to show the mission before it leaves.

options.label: Blame the Fund
options.description: Foreign accountants who have never wintered here. It plays well at home.

events.title: The Concert Sends a Delegation
events.description: Six officials, two interpreters and a list. The Concert wants procurement law, a court that answers to nobody, and a budget that adds up. In return it will say, in a communique, that Ardenia is on the right road.

options.label: Embrace the list
options.description: Promise all of it, on camera, and start on the easy half.

options.label: Push back on sovereignty
options.description: Ardenia did not leave one union to take dictation from another.

options.label: Thank them and file it
options.description: A good lunch, a firm handshake, no dates.

events.title: An Invitation From the East
events.description: The Union's secretariat has sent a letter, in two languages, inviting Ardenia to sit in as an observer. Cheaper gas is mentioned in the second paragraph. The word 'sovereignty' is not mentioned at all.

options.label: Take the observer's seat
options.description: A chair at the table, a flag in the corridor, and a Western ambassador who stops returning calls.

options.label: Show the letter to the West
options.description: Let the Concert read it first. Nothing makes a suitor attentive like a rival.

options.label: Decline with thanks
options.description: A polite reply that says not now and means not ever.

events.title: The Union Expects
events.description: The Union's council has a vote coming and a view on how Ardenia will cast it. The message arrived through the energy ministry, which is how everyone knows it is serious.

options.label: Vote with conscience
options.description: Cast the vote Ardenia would cast anyway, and wait for the bill.

options.label: Mention the door
options.description: Remind them that members can leave, and that leaving would be expensive for everyone.

options.label: Vote as expected
options.description: It is one vote. It will not be the last one.

events.title: Aid, Conditions Attached
events.description: A Western finance minister arrives with a cheque and a binder. The cheque relieves the debt. The binder is the price, and it is due in six months.

options.label: Take the money
options.description: Relief now, conditions later. Later always arrives.

options.label: Decline the binder
options.description: Ardenia will balance its own books, thank you.

events.title: The Binder Comes Due
events.description: Six months on, the donors want to see the conditions met: pension indexation suspended, the state holding company audited, the customs service purged. Their ambassador has a calendar.

options.label: Deliver the conditions
options.description: Do what was promised, and own every word of it in the regions.

options.label: Stall
options.description: Commissions, consultations, a working group. The donors have seen it before and claw back half.

events.title: Tanks at a Neighbour's Parliament
events.description: Overnight, soldiers took the radio station and the parliament of a fragile neighbour. A general read a statement about order. Every embassy in the capital wants to know what Ardenia will say.

options.label: Recognise the new authorities
options.description: Order on the border is worth more than a constitution that did not hold.

options.label: Condemn the coup
options.description: Ardenia knows what it costs when soldiers decide. Say so.

options.label: Wait and see
options.description: Coups have a way of ending in a second coup. Say nothing until it is clear who is answering the phone.

events.title: The Concert Is Counting Votes
events.description: The Concert is assembling a sanctions coalition against a state it has run out of patience with, and has asked Ardenia, politely and in writing, which side of the table it sits on.

options.label: Join the coalition
options.description: Stand with the Concert and pay for it in trade.

options.label: Speak against sanctions
options.description: Ardenia has lived under other people's embargoes. It will not join one.

options.label: Abstain
options.description: A small country's privilege: to be absent from the room.

events.title: An Offer of Arms
events.description: A friendly government has offered rifles, radios and armoured cars on easy terms. The Defense Ministry has already drafted the thank-you letter. The Finance Ministry has not.

options.label: Accept the arms
options.description: The army gets what it has asked for since 1992, and somebody across the line notices.

options.label: Decline politely
options.description: The army will make do. It always has.

events.title: Our Neighbour's "Legitimate Interests"
events.description: After its latest move against Ardenia, the old imperial neighbour has sent a note listing its 'legitimate interests': the language of the border districts, the pipeline's ownership, and who Ardenia may sign treaties with. It asks for a reply that recognises them.

options.label: Acknowledge their interests
options.description: Words cost little, and these words buy quiet. They also tell the West something.

options.label: Publish the note in the West
options.description: Let the Concert read what is being demanded of an applicant.

options.label: Reject the note
options.description: Ardenia's interests are Ardenia's. Send it back unanswered.

events.title: The Concert Offers to Build Faster
events.description: The Concert's energy commissioner has seen the second line's timetable and offers to put Western contractors and guarantees behind it. It would open a year and a half sooner. The commissioner mentions, in passing, that there will be conditions on the gas market.

options.label: Accept the Concert's help
options.description: Heat without the supplier's leave, eighteen months early. The supplier will read it as what it is.

options.label: Build it ourselves
options.description: Slower, and nobody else's line.

events.title: The Concert's Gas Conditions
events.description: The Concert's help with the second line came with a page about the gas market: unbundle the state gas company, publish the Zovar contract, and let Western suppliers bid. The commissioner would like to see progress.

options.label: Meet the conditions
options.description: Break up the gas company and publish the contract. The supplier's friends in the ministry will not forgive it.

options.label: Stall
options.description: A review of the review. The Concert slows its money to match.
